upheld.reason: The source n>=0 describes occupation-sequence length, including vacuum, whereas the fact quantifier is N>=1 for the number of available modes. It preserves that positive cutoff condition and the finite-support occupations from the source; no negative particle count or omitted vacuum is introduced.

Clause (b) of the source proves projection identities for every n>=1. The n>=2 phrase belongs only to clause (d) repeated-factor exclusion, which F2 does not use. The vacuum projection at n=0 is defined separately by the Fock direct-sum supplier.

The supplier starts with n>=1 and gives orthogonal symmetric projections in clause (b). Its later n>=2 condition qualifies only repeated-factor antisymmetry in clause (d). F1 uses projection and closed-range properties, with the scalar vacuum defined separately in the Statement.

The source says the form is independent of representatives of its two arguments: these are its two tensor vectors, not an arity restriction on each finite tensor expansion. The very same source displays the double finite-sum inner-product formula that F1 specializes to H and C^r.
